title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This handwritten page is written on the back of a typescript page of SGA 7 exposé IX (Néron models, monodromy). It is a scratch computation in linear duality between coalgebras/comodules and 'vectorial' functors. It fits the divided-power de Rham setting, where the dual of a divided-power algebra is a symmetric coalgebra and the reverse.

Notation. k is the base ring. For a k-module C, V(C) = Spec Sym(C), with points V(C)(A) = Hom_k(C, A).

Top diagram. S is a coalgebra with comultiplication Δ_S : S → S⊗S. γ : C → S is a coalgebra map, compatible with Δ_C and Δ_S (the vertical arrows). The composite C → C⊗C → C⊗S (via id_C⊗γ) makes C a right S-comodule.

Dualising:
- Since S is a coalgebra, V(S) is a monoid (algebra) functor under convolution.
- The coaction C → C⊗S gives an action V(C) × V(S) → V(C).
- He first writes 'V(S) anneau', strikes it, and writes 'V(S) opère sur V(C)'. He then asks whether V(C) carries a structure of algebra over V(S).

Bilinear maps. He considers maps V(C) × V(C') → V(C'') that are bilinear with respect to V(S), and seeks the comodule counterpart ('⊗ de comodules').
- Bilinear for k: a scheme map V(C)×V(C') → V(C'') is a linear map C'' → Sym(C)⊗Sym(C'). It is k-bilinear iff it factors through C⊗C', i.e. α : C'' → C⊗C'. (The intermediate guess C⊗Sym(C') is struck out.)
- Families: maps V(C)×Spec(A) → V(C'') linear in the first factor correspond to C'' → C⊗A. Compatibility with the S-action is a square C'' → C⊗A over C''⊗S → C⊗S⊗A.
- Balanced (middle-linear) condition: the square V(C)×V(S)×V(C') ⇉ V(C)×V(C') → V(C'') is dualised. It becomes (Δ_C⊗id_{C'})∘α = (id_C⊗Δ_{C'})∘α, i.e. α lands in the cotensor product C □_S C'.
- Equivariance: this common map also equals (α⊗id_S)∘Δ_{C''} (final square). So α is S-colinear.

Conclusion. V(S)-bilinear maps V(C)×V(C') → V(C'') correspond to comodule maps C'' → C □_S C'. Under duality, the tensor product of V(S)-modules corresponds to the cotensor product of S-comodules. This is a preparatory dictionary for describing structures (e.g. products and divided-power structures) on de Rham-type objects via linear schemes.
errors: No real errors. The page is exploratory, with several crossed-out false starts (e.g. 'anneau', C⊗Sym(C')).
Gap: with only a coaction C → C⊗S, the condition for V(S)-bilinearity requires both a right S-coaction on C and a left one on C'. These are written implicitly with the same symbols Δ_C, Δ_{C'}.
Gap: the duality V(C)(A) = Hom(C, A) behaves well only for flat or projective (or finite) modules. This is not discussed.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine scratch derivation of the standard comodule/module and cotensor/tensor duality for linear schemes. It is plausibly preparatory for the divided-power de Rham lecture but contains nothing new.
